passages.title: المحاكاة الأولى: سرّ المدينة العائمة
passages.text:
High in the Andes mountains of South America, straddling the border between Peru and Bolivia, lies Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world. At an elevation of more than 3,800 metres above sea level, the lake has been home to indigenous peoples for thousands of years. Among them, the Uros people are unique in that they do not live on the shore or on the mountainous islands; instead, they live on islands that they construct themselves – islands that float.

The Uros use the totora reed, a plant that grows abundantly in the shallow waters of the lake, as their primary construction material. The reeds are cut, dried, and then tightly bundled together to form a thick, buoyant base. This base is repeatedly layered until it can support the weight of several families and their simple homes, which are also made from the same reeds. The entire island is anchored with ropes to prevent it from drifting, yet it can be moved if necessary. Maintaining the island is a continuous task: fresh layers of reeds must be added every few weeks, especially during the rainy season, as the lower layers gradually rot away.

Historically, the Uros developed this extraordinary way of life as a defensive strategy. When the powerful Inca Empire expanded into their territory, the Uros retreated onto the lake, building their floating homes far from the shore, where they could not be easily attacked. Over the centuries, the Uros maintained their independence and distinct culture, even as the Inca and later the Spanish colonisers took control of the surrounding lands. Today, around 1,500 Uros still live on approximately 60 man‑made islands, preserving a tradition that has survived for at least 500 years.

In recent decades, however, the Uros’ way of life has come under threat. Climate change is altering the lake’s water levels and the growth patterns of the totora reeds. At the same time, the pull of modern urban life draws many young Uros away to nearby cities such as Puno in Peru or La Paz in Bolivia in search of education and employment. Tourism has become a double‑edged sword: on one hand, it provides a vital source of income for the remaining islanders; on the other, it risks turning a living culture into a museum exhibit. Anthropologists worry that without active intervention, the Uros’ unique floating world could disappear within a generation.

Despite the pressures, the Uros have shown remarkable resilience. In 2022, a team of Uros weavers created the largest floating textile ever recorded, measuring 450 square metres, which was displayed at an international art festival in Europe. The project not only brought global attention to their craft but also funded a new school on one of the islands, equipping the next generation with both traditional skills and modern knowledge. ‘We have always adapted,’ said one village elder. ‘The reeds taught us to bend without breaking. That is our secret.’

questions.q: 1. What is the main purpose of the first paragraph?
options: To describe the geography of the Andes
To introduce Lake Titicaca and explain why the Uros are unique
To explain how the Uros build their islands
questions.justification: الفقرة الأولى تُعرِّف ببحيرة تيتيكاكا وتُبرز تفرد شعب الأوروس الذي يعيش على جزر عائمة، مما يحدد موضوع القطعة.

questions.q: 2. The word 'buoyant' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to:
questions.justification: 'buoyant' تعني قادراً على الطفو، وهو المعنى المناسب لوصف قاعدة الجزيرة المصنوعة من القصب.

questions.q: 3. According to paragraph 3, why did the Uros originally build floating islands?
options: To escape from the Inca Empire
questions.justification: النص يوضح أن الأوروس انسحبوا إلى البحيرة لبناء منازل عائمة بعيداً عن الشاطئ كاستراتيجية دفاعية عند توسع إمبراطورية الإنكا.

questions.q: 4. What concern do anthropologists raise in the fourth paragraph?
options: Tourism has completely destroyed the Uros culture
Young Uros are building too many new islands
The Uros culture could vanish within a generation
The totora reeds are growing too fast
questions.justification: يذكر النص أن علماء الأنثروبولوجيا قلقون من أن عالم الأوروس العائم قد يختفي خلال جيل إذا لم يتم التدخل.

questions.q: 5. The word 'double‑edged sword' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to:
options: Something with both positive and negative effects
questions.justification: التعبير 'double‑edged sword' يُستخدم مجازاً لوصف شيء له فوائد وأضرار في آنٍ واحد، وهذا المقصود هنا بالسياحة.

questions.q: 6. Which of the following best describes the overall theme of the passage?
options: The dangers of tourism in South America
The adaptation and resilience of the Uros people
The environmental problems of Lake Titicaca
The history of the Inca Empire
questions.justification: القطعة بأكملها تركز على قدرة شعب الأوروس على التكيف والصمود عبر القرون في مواجهة التحديات.

passages.title: المحاكاة الثانية: لغز انهيار الحضارة الإيجية
passages.text:
The Minoan civilisation, which flourished on the island of Crete in the Aegean Sea from approximately 2700 to 1450 BCE, was one of the most advanced cultures of the ancient world. The Minoans built vast palace complexes, such as the one at Knossos, with sophisticated drainage systems and colourful wall paintings that depicted scenes of daily life and religious ceremonies. They were skilled sailors and traders whose ships dominated the eastern Mediterranean. Yet, by about 1450 BCE, their society had collapsed so completely that for centuries afterwards the Greeks could only speak of them in myths and legends.

For many decades, the dominant theory pointed to a single dramatic event: the eruption of the Thera volcano (modern‑day Santorini) around 1600 BCE. This was one of the largest volcanic explosions in human history, and it seemed logical to assume that a cataclysmic eruption, possibly followed by a tsunami, would have devastated the Minoan ports and palaces. The layer of volcanic ash that blanketed parts of the eastern Mediterranean was taken as further evidence of the destruction it must have caused. However, a closer examination of the archaeological record began to challenge this straightforward narrative.

Excavations in the late 20th century, particularly those led by the British archaeologist Sinclair Hood, revealed that Minoan cities had continued to flourish for at least 50 years after the Thera eruption. The ash layer was found lying beneath layers of rebuilt palaces, indicating that the Minoans had repaired the damage and resumed their way of life. This discovery forced historians to look for alternative explanations or to accept that the eruption, while certainly significant, could not have been the sole cause of the collapse. The real story, it now appears, is far more complex and frightening.

Current research suggests that the Minoans were the victims of a 'cascade' of interconnected disasters. The volcanic eruption may have triggered a series of large earthquakes that damaged buildings across Crete. Ash clouds probably altered weather patterns for several years, leading to widespread crop failure and famine. The disruption of trade routes would have isolated the island and made it difficult to import essential goods. Finally, weakened and disorganised, the Minoans were conquered by the Mycenaeans from mainland Greece, who occupied the damaged palace at Knossos and adapted Minoan writing for their own language.

Today, the fall of the Minoan civilisation serves as a powerful reminder of how even advanced societies can be brought down not by a single blow but by a combination of environmental and social pressures. Modern scientists study these ancient events to improve our understanding of natural hazards in the Mediterranean region. The story of the Minoans continues to evolve as new technologies, such as ground‑penetrating radar and DNA analysis of ancient seeds, uncover fresh evidence about the lives of these remarkable people. In many ways, the Minoans are still speaking to us – we just need to learn how to listen.

questions.q: 1. What were the Minoans particularly known for, according to the first paragraph?
options: Advanced palaces, drainage systems, and trade
questions.justification: تصف الفقرة الأولى القصور المعقدة، أنظمة الصرف المتطورة، والرسم على الجدران، بالإضافة إلى كونهم بحارة وتجاراً ماهرين.

questions.q: 2. What was the 'dominant theory' about the Minoan collapse mentioned in paragraph 2?
options: The eruption of the Thera volcano
questions.justification: الفقرة الثانية تشير مباشرة إلى النظرية السائدة التي ربطت الانهيار بثوران بركان ثيرا (سانتوريني).

questions.q: 3. Why did the 'volcano‑only' theory become doubtful?
options: No ash from Thera was ever found
Evidence showed the Minoans rebuilt and lived for decades after the eruption
The volcano was later proven to be a myth
questions.justification: الفقرة الثالثة توضح أن طبقة الرماد وُجدت تحت القصور المُعاد بناؤها، مما يدل على أن المينويين أصلحوا الأضرار واستمروا لعقود بعد الثوران.

questions.q: 4. The word 'cascade' in paragraph 4 is used to describe:
questions.justification: 'cascade' هنا مجازية، تصف سلسلة مترابطة من الكوارث المتتالية التي أدت إلى الانهيار.

questions.q: 5. Which group finally conquered the Minoans, according to the text?
questions.justification: تنص الفقرة الرابعة بوضوح على أن الميسينيين (Mycenaeans) هم من احتلوا القصر المتضرر في كنوسوس.

questions.q: 6. What is the main lesson the passage draws from the Minoan collapse?
options: That volcanoes are the only danger to civilisations
That Minoan art was not very good
That advanced societies can fall from multiple combined pressures
That trade routes are not important
questions.justification: الخاتمة تؤكد أن انهيارهم يُظهر كيف يمكن لمجتمع متقدم أن يسقط بفعل مجموعة من الضغوط البيئية والاجتماعية.

grammarQuestions.q: 304. Where is the manager? He……….. to other customers.
grammarQuestions.justification: السؤال عن حدث يحدث الآن، لذا نستخدم المضارع المستمر (is speaking).

grammarQuestions.q: 303. Neither Frank………..Tom graduates this year.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'neither ... nor ...' هي الأداة الصحيحة للنفي المزدوج.

grammarQuestions.q: 302. It is economic………….your money on cheap and good things.
grammarQuestions.justification: بعد الصفة 'economic' يأتي المصدر الكامل 'to spend' كفاعل مؤخر للجملة.

grammarQuestions.q: 301. She went home only to see the house…………upside down by her children.
grammarQuestions.justification: الحدث وقع قبل وصولها، لذا نستخدم Past Perfect Passive (had been turned).

grammarQuestions.q: 300. Whenever I travel to the UK, I…………….my cousins.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'Whenever' تدل على عادة متكررة، لذا Present Simple (visit).

grammarQuestions.q: 230. My father doesn’t speak Spanish. Neither ………….
grammarQuestions.justification: بعد 'neither' يأتي الفعل المساعد ثم الفاعل (does my mother).

grammarQuestions.q: 229. He was born ………. 1998.
grammarQuestions.justification: نستخدم 'in' مع السنوات.

grammarQuestions.q: 228. Did you enjoy yourselves?
grammarQuestions.justification: السؤال موجه بـ 'you' للجمع، لذا الإجابة 'Yes, we did'.

grammarQuestions.q: 227. They ……….. yesterday.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'yesterday' يدل على الماضي البسيط.

grammarQuestions.q: 226. I was …………..a shower when the phone rang.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'was taking' هي صيغة Past Continuous.

grammarQuestions.q: 225. ………….he was sick, he attended the lesson.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'Although' تستخدم للتناقض.

grammarQuestions.q: 224. If you want to be a doctor, you………go to the college of medicine.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'should' للنصيحة. 'ought' تحتاج إلى 'to'.

grammarQuestions.q: 223. Physics is the …………… of light and energy.
grammarQuestions.justification: يحتاج الفراغ إلى اسم (study) وليس فعلاً.

grammarQuestions.q: 222. Excuse me, could you ……………me the direction?
grammarQuestions.justification: بعد 'could' يأتي المصدر المجرد بدون to.

grammarQuestions.q: 221. If I …………a bird, I would fly away.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'If I were' تستخدم للحالة غير الواقعية.

grammarQuestions.q: 220. Mark walks …………… on the road.
grammarQuestions.justification: لوصف الفعل 'walks' نستخدم الظرف 'quietly'.

grammarQuestions.q: 219. He walked ……………. down the street.
grammarQuestions.justification: لوصف الفعل 'walked' نستخدم الظرف 'calmly'.

grammarQuestions.q: 218. The weather ………….. warm these days.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'these days' مع تغير تدريجي، لذا Present Continuous.

grammarQuestions.q: 217. He decided …………….. at home tonight.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'decide' يأتي بعده المصدر مع to.

grammarQuestions.q: 216. Our boss …………. important employees every Tuesday.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'every Tuesday' عادة متكررة، والفاعل مفرد، لذا 'meets'.

grammarQuestions.q: 215. Hinds language is good …….…... her brothers language is bad.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'but' للربط بين متناقضين.

grammarQuestions.q: 214. I want to buy a house …………. get married.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'in order to' تعبر عن الهدف.

grammarQuestions.q: 167. My sister is Anna, …………… is eighteen years old.
grammarQuestions.justification: ضمير الفاعل للعائدة على Anna هو 'she'.

grammarQuestions.q: 166. Russia is………….. than Canada.
grammarQuestions.justification: للمقارنة بين اثنين نستخدم الصفة + er بدون the.

grammarQuestions.q: 165. In our school they ………….. stay behind late if we didn’t do our homework.
grammarQuestions.justification: الفعل الرئيسي في الماضي (didn't)، لذا نستخدم 'made us'.

grammarQuestions.q: 164. Can you open the window? we need ……………...
grammarQuestions.justification: 'air' غير معدود، لذا لا نستخدم 'a'.

grammarQuestions.q: 163. Don’t take this book. It’s…………….
grammarQuestions.justification: 'mine' تعود على المتكلم، وتعني ملكي.

grammarQuestions.q: 162. What ……….. your job?
grammarQuestions.justification: للسؤال عن الوظيفة: 'What is your job?'

grammarQuestions.q: 161. I didn’t ………….. to the holiday last year.
grammarQuestions.justification: بعد 'didn’t' يأتي المصدر المجرد 'go'.

grammarQuestions.q: 160. Mohammad and Ahmed enjoy …….. while spending time together.
grammarQuestions.justification: الضمير الانعكاسي للغائبين هو 'themselves'.

grammarQuestions.q: 159. Ahmad's mother kept looking at him sympathetic while he ……… lectured by his father.
grammarQuestions.justification: الحدث كان مستمراً في الماضي، لذا Past Continuous Passive.

grammarQuestions.q: 158. Lexus cars ………….. by a Japanese company.
grammarQuestions.justification: السيارات تُصنع (مبني للمجهول) في المضارع: 'are made'.

grammarQuestions.q: 157. When I …………… the school, I ………….. shopping.
grammarQuestions.justification: حدثان ماضيان متتاليان: 'finished' ثم 'went'.

grammarQuestions.q: 156. My vacation is ………….. June 22.
grammarQuestions.justification: مع التواريخ نستخدم 'on'.

grammarQuestions.q: 155. Youssef lost his entire graduation project ………… his computer crashed.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'when' تربط بين الحدثين الزمنيين.

grammarQuestions.q: 393. My wife……………..the children when I got home.
grammarQuestions.justification: الحدث (إطعام الأطفال) وقع قبل وصولي، لذا Past Perfect.

grammarQuestions.q: 392. They respected…………..he said.
grammarQuestions.justification: 'what' تعني 'الشيء الذي'.

grammarQuestions.q: 391. ……………..him lately?
grammarQuestions.justification: 'lately' يدل على المضارع التام.

grammarQuestions.q: 390. The pilot landed the plane safely despite the fault of…..……….controls.
grammarQuestions.justification: الضمير يعود على 'the plane'، وهو غير عاقل مفرد، لذا 'its'.

grammarQuestions.q: 389. This book…………..by my father.
grammarQuestions.justification: مبني للمجهول ماضي: 'was written'.

grammarQuestions.q: 388. If it rains tomorrow, I……………...a raincoat.
grammarQuestions.justification: First Conditional: if + present, will + infinitive.

vocabularyQuestions.q: She went home only to see that the house…………upside down by her children.
vocabularyQuestions.justification: Past Perfect Passive تدل على حدث وقع قبل وصولها.
